This is irritable bowel syndrome, which involves the colon. Its sympathetic supply comes from preganglionic neurons in the intermediolateral cell column of the thoracolumbar spinal cord (about T10–L2), which reach the gut through the splanchnic nerves and synapse in the prevertebral ganglia. The midgut portion (to the mid-transverse colon) is supplied via the lesser and least thoracic splanchnic nerves to the superior mesenteric ganglion, and the hindgut portion via the lumbar splanchnic nerves to the inferior mesenteric ganglion.

CONFIDENCE: 82
